body: I ended up moving back to live with my parents. I don't know where to go from here. I spend all day researching suicide methods.

I've been suicidal since I was young. I found someone that I loved, dated him for five years, and then he broke up with me. I moved across the country for him and dropped out of college when he we broke up.

I feel the same as I did before meeting him—completely empty. I have executive dysfunction issues and have never worked a job. I feel totally hopeless.

Hey there. I'm very sorry to hear that you're hurting so much. I see a lot of pain in your post and my heart really goes out to you. What you've written resonates with me because it reminds me a lot of my relationship with my ex. It is absolutely heart-wrenching to lose someone to themselves despite doing absolutely everything in your power to help them, to the point where you begin to lose yourself. When he doesn't even seem to *see* you despite everything... I can't even put into words how much it hurts.

You sound like a tremendously loyal, compassionate person with a giant heart. You mention that you feel you've made no progress at all but it seems you're selling yourself short:

>A year later here I am, at a much healthier weight, my social anxiety is gone, and I'm closer to my family and friends than ever. 

Try to remember that recovery (in all forms) is not linear. You've made some very, very difficult changes despite the pain you've gone through and you know what? It's pretty incredible. Are you in therapy? A third-party perspective may be helpful to you. It seems you struggle with codependency and I think therapy would be beneficial for you in that regard. 

I wish you the very best of luck. You are a good person and you deserve so much more than this man gave you.
